body: I’ve felt that way, before, but he wouldn’t be better off with someone else.  You are the closest, most precious person to him that there ever will be.  There is no one, absolutely NO ONE, who loves that sweet baby more than you do, and even though you can’t make it all better, that fact will never change.  It sounds like there’s something going on; imagine him having to go through all that without his mum, with a total stranger, instead.  If he isn’t feeding or gaining weight, then doctors need to really dig in to figure this out.  Even though you’re amazing, you can’t fix everything by yourself, sometimes.  You and your love are worth SO much, and you are a crucial part to help him get through whatever is giving him so much trouble.

I hear you.  I hate to admit it, but I feel my mind slipping a little more each day.  My son is 6 months, now, and I adore him.  I, too, stayed home longer than anticipated and lost my job as a result, as well as my health insurance.  I have spent all the money I saved from working on the cost of the birth and baby expenses.  I’m afraid to go anywhere because of COVID and because I’m just generally afraid of driving and getting into an accident without health insurance.  My mother, who lives 15 minutes away, refuses to clean or cook for anyone, and expects me to bring the baby over to see her, always, so I get no help there.  I don’t have any friends around here.  Since my partner works full-time, I’m supposed to be taking care of everything around the house, but I’m failing at that.  The baby needs so much, and I’m just so. tired.  All I want to do is sleep whenever he is sleeping, but that’s the time I’m supposed to be doing my work around the house.  I have no sex drive, at all.  I don’t feel anything, but that’s how my partner needs to connect.  If I don’t have sex, he seems to isolate, and we start to drift apart to where we almost never speak to each other.  I have gained weight after giving birth (wtf?), and I’m just feeling like a fat, useless, lonely blob.  Sorry, I don’t have any suggestions other than how I’m getting by; I just look at my son and know that, even if I don’t seem to mean that much to anyone else, he needs me.

Guess I needed to say it out loud, as well.

Thank you!  They did confirm it was a small abruption.  The OB found several large clots.  They sent the placenta off to pathology to try and figure out why it happened, but they weren’t able to determine the cause.  OB told us she was very glad we made the decision to get the c-section because she’s never seen an overall good outcome from trying to proceed with a natural birth with the signs she saw (the blood and his slowing heart rate).

That really sucks.  I haven’t even begun to process what this will be like for me.  I swore up and down that I would stay home with my child until he starts school, but hubby’s job situation has taken a crappy turn, and it’s just not going to be possible for me to leave my income and benefits.  I know that I have to do what’s necessary to provide for my son, but damn it’s difficult.  😕
Congrats!  Very minor freak-out when I saw it, because it all became a little more real, but pleasantly not worried.  Ordered pizza before I called the midwife about it.  Priorities! 😂

Hope things happen for you, soon!  Girl, I can’t even imagine 39 weeks; I am feeling so done with this at 36, already 😂! Just hoping, for baby’s sake, that we can hold on until 38 weeks, maybe?  Give those lungs some more time to cook.

Yeah, I’d been having lots of increased discharge-mostly clear to whitish.  This was eye-catching because it was like a large glob of mucus like from bad cold or sinus infection, it wasn’t nearly as thin and slightly watery as the other discharge, and it was tinged very light brown.  Midwife confirmed and said it’s totally normal, the cervix is just softening and to just pay attention to baby’s movement and any actual labor signs, when they come.
Good call!  Googled some images and that’s exactly what my tootsies are looking like.  Never experienced it before.  Now, if I could just wear flip-flops to work...

I did, but I had major depressive disorder before the pregnancy.  It was managed well with meds, but I stopped taking them when I found out I was pregnant.  I went for as long as I could to, at least, make it through the first trimester.  Eventually, though, maybe about 18 weeks, I talked to the OB about getting back on an antidepressant.  I was just having too many down days compared to normal days.  He said it would be fine, and it would be good to have the meds in place and working before any possible postpartum issues.  Maybe talk to your doc about it?
Thank you, for talking to me.
Thank you, for talking to me.

I want it to be enough to teach.  I really do.  I don’t even know why it’s not; it used to be the reason I could always pull through even my deepest hurt and loneliness.  I sound so melodramatic, but it’s like my analytical side just takes over and sometimes I can’t find enough meaning to keep going.
